title: Hosted endpoint release gates and scope synthesis for gen/embeddings/rerank
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Synthesize final PRD acceptance criteria, release gates and scope cut decisions for the hosted endpoint bundle (generation / chat, embeddings, rerank). This ticket captures the minimal behavioral contract, cross-team dependency orchestration, canary measurement thresholds, and the pre-launch checklist operators and PMs must verify before go-live.
goals: Define clear release gate pass/fail criteria tied to telemetry (latency, p50/p95, error rate, cost per token)
Agree on a minimal behavioral contract across gen, embeddings and rerank to avoid late scope creep
Document inter-team dependencies and required artifacts (runtime pins, SDK compatibility, canary dashboards)
Produce an actionable pre-launch checklist that engineers, SRE and support can follow for a clean cutover
out_of_scope: Full multi-region active/active migration for Dedicated customers
New model training or model architecture changes
Large-scale UI redesign of Console dashboards (minor telemetry views only)
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral contract doc published and signed off by Product, Runtime, and SDK leads
Deterministic acceptance harness with 250 synthetic prompts (covering generation, embeddings, rerank) runs green against canary model set
Latency SLOs verified: p50 <= 120ms for small-gen lane, p95 <= 900ms for heavy-gen lane under canary traffic profile
Error budget check: canary error rate < 0.05% for 30m rolling window otherwise automatic rollback
Cost-per-token estimate validated within +/- 20% of projection under canary workload
KV prefix cache correctness tests pass with 100% key consistency for 1M synthetic keys
SDK compatibility: JavaScript and Python SDK smoke tests pass with pinned API contract
Telemetry and alerting hooks present in Console and linked to runbook (oncall, escalation, postmortem owner)
rollout_plan: Three-phase canary: (1) internal-only test lane (10% synthetic), (2) seeded partner tenants (5 tenants, <1% traffic), (3) gradual ramp to 50% then 100% over 48h with automated gating. Each phase must pass telemetry checks and acceptance harness. Rollback policy defined: automatic rollback on SLO breaches or manual rollback if functional regressions found.
prelaunch_checklist: Runtime: release build tagged and validated on dedicated canary cluster
Models: model variants and quantization profiles pinned in artifact registry
SDKs: JS/Python packages published to canary channel and smoke-tested
Console: canary dashboards created and shared with stakeholders
Telemetry: synthetic probe alerts configured for latency, errors, and cost anomalies
Security: KMS integration verification for Private deployments and SSO smoke test
Documentation: PRD, behavior catalog and developer migration notes published
Support: runbook and escalation routes communicated, postmortem owner assigned
risks: Late behavioral regressions detected in rerank causing customer ranking differences
Underestimated token cost for long-context generation leading to budget overshoot
KV cache edge cases causing stale prefix hits in production
SDK consumers relying on undocumented response fields may break
Telemetry gaps that delay detection of P95 latency regressions
mitigations: Lock down behavioral contract fields for this release; any additions require explicit PM+Eng signoff
Run extended cost simulation with 10x long-context samples and cap early ramp if cost deviates >20%
Add end-to-end cache invalidation tests and run across canary tenants
Provide a temporary compatibility shim for deprecated response fields in SDKs
Add an extra 6h observation window after each ramp step before proceeding
decision_log: 2025-02-15: Agreed to freeze additional output-format changes during canary (decision by Runtime + SDK leads)
2025-02-20: Opted for three-phase canary with seeded partner tenants to get realistic signals (decision by PM)
2025-02-25: Scoped out multi-region Dedicated rollout for a later milestone; not required for initial hosted launch
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: PRD initial draft posted; requested feedback from Runtime and SRE teams
2025-02-18: Runtime completed kernel selection validation for pinned models; minor perf tweaks required
2025-02-22: SDK team published canary packages; JS smoke test failed for streaming boundary case (investigating)
2025-02-27: Canary dashboard prototype created; trace sampling rate increased to 100% for canary hosts
2025-02-28: Acceptance harness test corpus expanded to include 26 new long-context prompts for cost profiling
qa_checks: Run acceptance harness against canary for 24h and ensure no functional regressions
Execute load profile runs at 1x, 2x, and 4x expected canary QPS to validate queueing behavior
End-to-end encryption verification for Private deployment path
Manual verification of conversational determinism for 50 seed prompts
Contract fuzzing on response schema to detect unexpected fields or missing keys
post_launch_checks: 72h health sweep for top 10 customers and partner tenants
Cost reconciliation report for first 24h and 7d windows
Collect qualitative feedback from seeded partners and surface to Product
Run post-deploy regression evals on flagged prompt sets and file bugs
notes: This PRD emphasizes deterministic acceptance tests to reduce subjective signoffs at launch
Keep scope cuts small: prefer disabling non-critical rerank features over delaying the release
If a security review identifies a blocking finding, the release will be paused until mitigations are deployed
